evidence.finding: Candidate kernel (Block Dim 1024, Task Duration 255453 us) per-block mean aiv_time 9824.9 us with min 9787.1 / max 9847.1 across all 1024 blocks: every program executes identical work and per-block time is uniform. Per block only ~32 KB of output is produced (128 serial iterations x 256 B), yet aiv_mte3_instructions=8193 (8192 per block, ~128 B per instruction) and write_main_memory_datas=1024 KB per block (32x the bytes the program actually has to write), while aiv_main_mem_write_bw is only 0.099 GB/s per block and read BW ~0.008 GB/s (sum over blocks ~8 GB/s). Pipe use: aiv_vec_ratio 0.5387, mte2_ratio 0.0010, mte3_ratio 0.1038, vec_wait_ratio 0.1510. So the cost is instruction/memory-op fragmentation at tiny granularity, not HBM/L2 bandwidth.

Compiled with BLOCK_X=128, BLOCK_Y=1 for the target case. Program maps only over spatial output; all N*C planes are handled by nested scf.for loops (128 serial iterations). Output row/column indices are produced by arith.remsi (`(pid_x*BLOCK_X+arange) % OW`), so the store offsets are a 2-D tensor<1x128> whose contiguity/alignment the compiler cannot prove; the IR keeps tensor<1x128> pointer arithmetic with mixed i32/i64 and the store is emitted from that wrapped index tensor.

Target case upsample_bilinear2d-timing-1: 253.949 ms vs reference 0.2455 ms (speedup 0.00097x); timing-0/2/4 are ~8.6-9.9 ms and timing-3/5 ~256-294 ms. 6 of 24 formal cases fail with MLIRCompilationError in ConvertTritonIRToLinalgIR (correctness-2,3,8,9,14,15), i.e. part of the contract does not even compile.

All 16 tuned configs keep BLOCK_X in {64..512} and BLOCK_Y in {1,2} with num_warps 4/8: the supplied tuning space never expresses a full-output-row tile, so the retile mechanism I test is outside the supplied search space rather than a repetition of it.

record.hypothesis: The 254 ms on the target case is set by per-program instruction count, not by occupancy or bandwidth: the kernel writes its 128-element row chunk through a `% OW`-wrapped, shape-[1,128] index tensor, so Triton-Ascend emits ~8192 tiny mte3 stores (and ~8192 mte2 loads) per program with ~128 B granularity and ~32x write amplification, and every program additionally replays a 128-iteration serial N*C loop over that fragmented index pattern. Retiling to (plane, row-block, column-block) with explicit block indices plus a bounds mask instead of modular wrap should let the compiler prove the full-width row store is contiguous/aligned and emit a few wide DMAs instead of thousands of tiny ones.
record.change: Single mechanism: retile programs. Replace the spatial-only grid + `% OW`/`% OH` index wrap + serial N*C loop with a 3-D grid (column block, row block, plane = n*C+c), full-width row tiles whose column index is `pid*BLOCK_W + arange` plus an explicit `ow < OW`/`oh < OH` mask, and 2-D [BLOCK_H, BLOCK_W] weights/taps computed from the same formulas. Per-element math (fp32 coordinate mapping, clamping, 2-D bilinear weights, fp32 accumulation order) is kept identical. Compatibility edits (recorded separately from performance): (a) move the align_corners ratio (IH-1)/(OH-1) computation to the host in Python and feed it as a float kernel argument so no integer division appears in the kernel (the align_corners branch currently fails ConvertTritonIRToLinalgIR on 6 formal cases); (b) add the required public entrypoint alias `run(input, output_size, align_corners=False, scales_h=None, scales_w=None)` next to the preserved FlagGems `upsample_bilinear2d`. No caching, no host-side computation of tensor values.
record.expected: If the diagnosis holds, the candidate kernel's mte3 instruction count per program drops from thousands to a handful of wide stores and the 32x write amplification disappears; target-case full-call time should drop by at least an order of magnitude from 253.95 ms (expected tens of ms or below), with the target still correct. The 6 previously non-compiling align_corners cases should start running. Gather loads (4 taps per output element) remain and are expected to become the next visible limit; if time stays near 254 ms and per-block mte3 counts stay ~8000, this mechanism is falsified.
record.validation: Preflight: source review + compile of the edited candidate. Then the host formal evaluation over the 24 formal cases plus supplementary and CANN supplementary checks; compare per-case latency and pass count with baseline-evaluation.json, and confirm the align_corners cases now compile and match within atol/rtol 0.015 at required_matched_ratio 1.0. No re-collected paired profiling is available from this call, so the mte3-instruction prediction stays an expectation, not a measurement.
alternatives: The kernel is HBM/L2-bandwidth-bound: contradicted by aiv_main_mem_write_bw 0.099 GB/s and aiv_main_mem_read_bw 0.008 GB/s per block (sum ~100 and ~8 GB/s), far below device capability, and by mte2_ratio 0.0010.

The serial N*C loop starves parallelism: contradicted by uniform per-block aiv_time (min 9787 us, max 9847 us) over 1024 blocks; the machine is already fully occupied and total time is waves x per-program time, so only per-program work/instruction count can reduce the total.
record.discriminating_observation: Per block: only ~32 KB of output exists, but mte3 instruction count is 8193 (~128 B per instruction) and write_main_memory_datas is 1024 KB (32x amplification), while block time is perfectly uniform across all 1024 blocks (~9.8 ms). Together these separate 'fragmented tiny memory ops per program' from both a bandwidth limit and an occupancy limit.

evidence.finding: Candidate kernel 'upsample_bilinear2d_kernel' Task Duration = 255453.4 us for timing-1, while the CANN reference completes the same operator in 169.1 us (ResizeBilinearV2) + small casts/transdata. Per-block AccountingUtilization aiv_time mean = 9824.9 us and aiv_total_cycles mean = 16.21M for 1024 block rows (~126k cycles per iteration of the kernel's inner N*C loop), i.e. the cost is inside the kernel body, not launch/autotune: the harness latency 253.9 ms matches the kernel task duration.

All four tl.load sites with data-dependent column indices (offset_00/01/10/11) are lowered to scalar scf.for loops over the 128 vector lanes containing one memref.load per element, tagged {DiscreteMemAccess}/{ExtractedLoadOrStore}, and the whole float index derivation (remsi on i64, sitofp, addf, mulf, subf, maxnumf, fptosi, minsi) is re-executed per lane inside that loop. The tl.store is lowered the same way (one bufferization.materialize_in_destination per lane). Consequence: 5 general-memory accesses per output element are scalar and their address math is scalar, so the vector unit cannot be used for the data movement.

Real-device selected config for timing-1 is BLOCK_X=128, BLOCK_Y=1, num_warps=8 (i.e. one output row per program, oh/real_h scalar). The dominant source_loop region (candidate lines 105-130) contains the four load sites, each followed by BAR and WAIT_FLAG on the VECTOR/SCALAR pipes; SCALARLDST has 20788 events and the SCALAR pipe spends 26.6 us of 72.2 us in waits. The capture is explicitly a partial window (application did not finish), so it can only support the per-iteration structure, not a total-duration or speedup claim.

Starter result: 18/24 formal cases pass; correctness cases 2,3,8,9,14,15 fail with MLIRCompilationError (ConvertTritonIRToLinalgIR pass failure); all six timing cases run, timing-1 = 253.95 ms versus 0.2455 ms reference. This is the source that must not be regressed.

Native tuned config list for upsample_bilinear2d covers BLOCK_X in {64,128,256,512} x BLOCK_Y in {1,2} with num_warps in {4,8}; program_id is read through FlagGems triton_lang_extension. No task-specific optimization knowledge is supplied (knowledge.json mechanisms empty).

record.hypothesis: The 255 ms is caused by the access formulation, not by grid serialization alone: because every input address depends on a data-dependent column index (w0/w1 computed by float floor of the rescaled coordinate) and every output address contains '(pid_x*BLOCK_X + arange) % OW', the Ascend lowering scalarizes all four loads and the store into per-lane memref.load/memref.store loops and also re-executes the float coordinate/index arithmetic per lane (~2k cycles per produced element, 16.2M cycles per block). For the target case the scale is exactly 2, where the mapping is piecewise affine: output row 2i = 0.25*in[i-1]+0.75*in[i], row 2i+1 = 0.75*in[i]+0.25*in[i+1], and the same pair of weights applies horizontally, so the four gathers can be replaced by contiguous (affine) shifted loads of the same input rows and contiguous pair stores, with no data-dependent address at all.
record.change: Add a self-contained exact-2x fast path kernel (upsample_bilinear2d_2x_kernel) selected purely from runtime metadata (align_corners False, OH == 2*IH, OW == 2*IW, reciprocal scale exactly 0.5 for both axes), which (a) parallelizes (n,c) on program_id(2) and the input row on program_id(1) instead of an in-kernel N*C loop, (b) replaces the four data-dependent gathers by nine contiguous shifted row loads (offsets j-1, j, j+1) with boundary clamping done by tl.where in registers, and (c) writes the two output rows as contiguous (BLOCK_J,2) column pairs (even = 0.25*v[j-1]+0.75*v[j], odd = 0.75*v[j]+0.25*v[j+1]) so all addresses are affine. The generic FlagGems kernel and its autotune path are kept byte-for-byte for every other case, so all non-2x formal/supplementary cases behave exactly as the starter. Compatibility edits are separate: add a 'run' alias with the same signature as upsample_bilinear2d (public_entrypoint) in addition to the existing exported name, and no change to the FlagGems imports used by the generic path.
record.expected: For upsample_bilinear2d-timing-1 the kernel Task Duration should drop from ~255 ms to the order of a few ms (target >10x, plausibly 30-100x) because no general-memory access remains data-dependent; per-block aiv_time should fall from 9.8 ms to tens of microseconds. Correctness must stay bit-comparable within the 0.015 atol/rtol contract (2x weights 0.25/0.75 are exact and fp32 accumulation order differs by at most a few ulps). Non-2x cases are routed to the unchanged generic kernel, so their pass/fail status must be unchanged (18/24 plus the same 6 compile failures unless those cases are themselves exact 2x).
record.validation: Preflight (bridge) must compile the new source. Then host full formal evaluation: 24 correctness cases and the supplementary checks, plus timing case 1 vs the 253.9 ms starter latency. If the fast path is taken by some supplementary case, its result must stay inside the frozen tolerances. Follow-up: re-capture paired profiling/IR for the new source to confirm the loads/stores are no longer emitted as per-lane memref.load loops and to re-measure per-block aiv_time.
alternatives: The cost is dominated by the serial N*C loop (only 128 output elements per iteration) rather than by the scalarized accesses; if so, only moving (n,c) into the grid would give a large speedup and an affine-load rewrite would add little.

The cost is dominated by launch/autotune host work rather than device time; contradicted by the 255453 us kernel Task Duration matching the 253.9 ms harness latency, but the harness may still include per-call Python/launch overhead that a kernel-side change cannot remove.
The remsi/modulo and int64 address arithmetic alone account for most of the cost; then removing only the modulo (affine store) would already recover most of the time.
The 6 MLIRCompilationError cases are caused by constructs I am not touching (e.g. the align_corners branch), so they will persist after this change.
record.discriminating_observation: The bcmlir shows the loads and the store as per-lane scalar loops with per-lane index recomputation, while the same kernel's vector-unit pipelines show only ~65% VECTOR activity and a 9.8 ms per-block residence: the wall time is ~1978 cycles per produced output element, which is only explicable by scalarized general-memory access plus scalar address math, not by the loop trip count alone (128 iterations) and not by launch overhead (kernel Task Duration equals harness latency). The simulator adds the concrete per-iteration structure (BLOCK_Y=1 selected; four load sites each followed by BAR/WAIT_FLAG) and, importantly, warns that its window is partial so it cannot be used to rank the loads by total time; the affine-vs-serialized distinction is settled by the bcmlir, not by the simulator.
